oauth.alternatives: For reading a user's feed, messages, connections or other people's profiles, the official open permissions give no path. Options: stick to profile, email and posting; apply to a partner program if your use case fits Marketing, Talent or Learning; or ask users to export their own data. Avoid scraping, which breaks LinkedIn's terms.

appTypes.name: Standard developer app (one type)
appTypes.whenToUse: One multi-user app holds your client ID and secret. Every user connects their own account through it. Product access is attached to the app, not to a user tier.

verdict.label: Gated
verdict.summary: Any user can connect for profile, email and posting (w_member_social) without review, but reading anything else, which an inbox-style agent needs, requires a partner program that LinkedIn can refuse. Programmatic refresh tokens are also limited to approved partners.
verdict.nextStep: Create an app at https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps and add the Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect and Share on LinkedIn products.
verdict.customerSideGateNote: Nothing found requiring a customer admin to approve a member-scoped app. Not confirmed for Page or Ads scopes.

composio.note: Composio lists LinkedIn under its managed OAuth apps, so you can start today. Moving to your own app later affects new connections only. Existing users must reconnect.

stages.name: Prototype (open products)
stages.whoCanConnect: Any LinkedIn member who consents, for the open scopes openid, profile, email and w_member_social. No test-user list or user cap was found in the docs.
stages.notes: Access tokens last 60 days and no refresh token is issued unless you are a partner. Plan a re-consent every 60 days.

stages.name: Limited (partner product requested)
stages.whoCanConnect: Only apps that hold the approved product. Requests for gated products stay pending until reviewed.
stages.notes: No official review time was found. Unofficial blogs claim 3 to 6 months for partner approval, which is unverified. Access requests expire after 21 days if not completed. Hours are our estimate.

stages.name: Production (any user, gated scopes)
stages.whoCanConnect: Any member, for the scopes your approved products grant.
stages.notes: Only possible for use cases that fit a partner program. Sign-in and posting need no review. Hours are our estimate.

scopeTiers.name: Open (self-serve)
scopeTiers.effect: Identity, primary email and the member's own posts, comments and likes. Not a read path for feed, messages or connections.

scopeTiers.name: Marketing (Advertising API, Audiences)
scopeTiers.effect: Approval is needed. MDP partners can use programmatic refresh tokens (60-day access, 365-day refresh).

scopeTiers.name: Sales, Talent, Compliance
scopeTiers.effect: SNAP or Talent partner approval. Compliance is closed and may not be requested.

requirements.item: LinkedIn developer app with client ID and secret
requirements.detail: Create it in the developer portal. Open products are added from the Products tab.
Absolute URL, no # fragment, query parameters are ignored. Must match a registered URL.

requirements.item: LinkedIn Page you admin, linked to the app
requirements.detail: Community sources say app creation asks for a Page and page admin verification. The official pages I read do not state this.

requirements.item: Use case that fits a partner program
requirements.detail: Marketing, Talent, Sales or Learning. Other use cases are unlikely to be approved.

requirements.item: Live privacy policy, use-case description and product demo
requirements.detail: Reported for partner access forms by third-party guides. Confirm in the portal form.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Open https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps, sign in, click Create app, and fill in name, logo and privacy policy URL. Select a LinkedIn Page you admin if asked.

steps.title: Add open products
steps.detail: On the app's Products tab, add Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect and Share on LinkedIn. The Auth tab then lists the scopes.

steps.title: Register the redirect URL
steps.detail: On the Auth tab, add your HTTPS callback. Copy the client ID and secret into your server config.

steps.title: Send members to the authorize URL
steps.detail: Use https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, state and scope=openid profile email w_member_social.

steps.title: Exchange the code
steps.detail: POST to https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken within 30 minutes of getting the code. Store the 60-day access token and its expiry.

steps.title: Build re-consent for day 60
steps.detail: Without partner refresh tokens, send users through the flow again before expiry. The consent screen is skipped if they are still logged in to linkedin.com and the token is unexpired.

steps.title: Decide if you need gated data
steps.detail: If you need ads, Pages, or recruiting data, add the matching product on the Products tab and complete the access form.

steps.title: Submit and watch the 21-day window
steps.detail: Expired or declined requests can be resubmitted with the Reapply button in the portal.

steps.title: Ask for programmatic refresh tokens
steps.detail: These are for approved MDP partners. Ask through the Developer Support request form after approval.

steps.title: Move users off the Composio app
steps.detail: Switch to your own client ID. Existing Composio connections must reconnect.

blockers.symptom: 401 Invalid scope on the authorize request
blockers.cause: The scope is not provisioned for your app because the product is not added or approved.
blockers.fix: Add the product on the Products tab and request only scopes listed on the Auth tab.

blockers.cause: The redirect URL differs from the registered one, or has a fragment.
blockers.fix: Register the exact absolute HTTPS URL and send the same value in both calls.

blockers.symptom: Users must sign in again about every 60 days
blockers.cause: Access tokens last 60 days and refresh tokens are for approved partners only.
blockers.fix: Build a re-consent prompt, or pursue MDP partner approval if you qualify.

blockers.symptom: invalid_request: refresh token invalid, expired or revoked
blockers.cause: The refresh token expired after 365 days, or LinkedIn revoked it.
blockers.fix: Send the member through the normal authorization flow again.

blockers.cause: Requests expire after 21 days or are declined for thin detail.
blockers.fix: Use Reapply in the Products page, add detail, and contact Developer Support through the request form.

blockers.symptom: Existing tokens stop working after you change scopes
blockers.cause: Requesting a different scope invalidates earlier access tokens.
blockers.fix: Ask users to reauthorize whenever your scope set changes.

drafts.title: Share on LinkedIn (w_member_social)
drafts.body: Our app lets a member draft and publish posts to their own LinkedIn profile. We request w_member_social only to create, comment on and like posts at the member's explicit request. We request openid, profile and email only to identify the member and show their name and photo. We do not read other members' data or post without the member's confirmation. Members can disconnect at any time in our settings and in LinkedIn permissions.

drafts.title: Partner access demo
drafts.body: 1. Show the app homepage and privacy policy URL. 2. Click Connect LinkedIn and show the consent screen with your app name and logo. 3. Show the scopes requested. 4. Perform the one action that uses each scope. 5. Show disconnect and data deletion. 6. State how long tokens are stored and who can access them.

evidence.claim: LinkedIn API uses OAuth 2.0 for member authorization, with 3-legged and 2-legged flows.
Sign In with LinkedIn uses OIDC with openid, profile and email scopes.
evidence.sourceTitle: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect

evidence.claim: Redirect URLs must be absolute HTTPS and registered; code lives 30 minutes; access tokens last 60 days; changed scopes invalidate old tokens; scopes depend on products; invalid scope and redirect errors.
Only profile, email and w_member_social are open to all developers; most other permissions and partner programs need approval; Compliance is closed; SNAP and Talent need partner approval.
Standard refresh is re-running authorization; the consent screen is skipped if the member is logged in and the token is unexpired; programmatic refresh tokens are for a limited set of partners.
Since May 2026, expired (after 21 days) or declined API access requests can be reapplied in the portal; Developer Support moved to a request form from May 15, 2026.
evidence.note: Seen in a search result snippet for this official page, which I did not open with fetch_page.

evidence.claim: Programmatic refresh tokens are for approved MDP partners: 60-day access, 365-day refresh, LinkedIn may revoke at any time.

evidence.note: Only unofficial, unopened search results mention a 3 to 6 month cycle; no official timeline was found, so waits are left unbounded.
